Just an update to my previous woes.

I noticed that another module in sna, utils.c also used ISNAN, but when I compiled by hand, it completed successfully. Sadly, my coding knowledge is limited.

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Distance Statistic
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sean.   Good question -- I forgot that most users of R packages use  
the pre-compiled binary versions that are automatically provided by  
CRAN.  You must instead obtain the source code for the ergm package to  
find the files I refer to below.  To do this, you'll need to visit the  
r-project.org website, then choose a CRAN mirror and find ergm in the  
list of packages.  You'll find a couple pre-compiled binaries along  
with the source code (the latter is in a tarred and gzipped file; see  
below).

If you're using a PC, then Duncan Murdoch's website at http://www.murdoch-sutherland.com/Rtools/ 
  is a must-read if you're going to play with source code.

If you're on a mac or linux, you can type
tar xfz XXX.tar.gz
in a terminal window in order to expand a tarred and gzipped directory  
called XXX.tar.gz.  If you're on windows, then I think you'll be able  
to do the same thing from a DOS window after you install the tools at  
Murdoch's website.

Hope this helps.
Dave

messages.subject: [statnet_help] optim() in latentnet throws warnings
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I try to fit a latent space model with the ergmm() function of latentnet.
Within the ergmm() function an optim() function is called with control  
= "control", where "control" is a list with parameters not known by  
optim().

Over 50 warning messages of the following type are thrown:

"In optim(par = start.vals, fn = optim.fs$f, gr = optim.fs$grad.f,  ... :
   unknown names in control: sample.size, burnin, interval, threads,  
mle.maxit, Z.delta, group.deltas, pilot.runs,........."


How did I generate this problem?

1. Newly install version R-2.9.0 on a windows computer
2. > install.packages("statnet")
3. > library("statnet")
4. > data("sampson")
5. > samplike.fit <- ergmm(samplike ~ latent(d = 2), tofit = c("mle"),  
verbose=1)
6. > warnings() --> gives the above warning-messages.
In addition:
7. > summary(samplike.fit) --> throws Error: "Error in  
summary.ergmm(samplike.fit) :   MCMC was not was not run for this fit."

Does statnet have an own optim() function, which should be in the  
search path before the optim() of the stats package?

However, when I do search(), all statnet related packages are before  
the package stats. The same warnings/errors are produced when  
library("latentnet") is loaded instead of library("statnet").

Does anybody have a suggestion how to resolve the problem?

Thank you very much
Moritz Mueller

messages.subject: [statnet_help] sna 2.0 Released
messages.body_plain:
At long last, version 2.0 of sna has now been released (and should be 
gradually percolating through the CRAN mirror sites).  As foretold, the 
new version has many new features, substantial performance enhancements, 
improved interoperability with network and SparseM, support for a new 
edgelist data type, and a few other changes.

Package information (including the ChangeLog) can be found at 
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sna/index.html.  Thanks go to 
everyone whose suggestions, pokes, and prodding since the last release 
helped in guiding this one.  (Special thanks also to Alex Montgomery, 
for his input and multiple contributions to the latest revision of gplot.)

Enjoy,

-Carter

messages.subject: [statnet_help] preferential attachement
messages.body_plain:
Dear list,

I am trying to generate a network matrice similar to the barabasi.game 
function.

But the network should be different to the network generated by the 
barabasi.game function in a way that existing nodes can also form in 
each period new connections among each other based on mechanisms similar 
to preferential attachements. In addition the network should be directed 
and not symetric!

That means I am looking for a combination of preferential attachement 
and preferential update. Are there possibilities to generate such a 
network using the statnet packages in R?

Thanks for your help and best regards from Switzerland

Florian

messages.subject: [statnet_help] preferential attachement
messages.body_plain:
There is nothing in statnet that will do this automatically, though it  
shouldn't be hard to program by hand.  That said, I'm afraid I  
wouldn't have time to help implement it.
The basic idea would be to create a network object containing all of  
the nodes you'd want at the end, then start adding edges one by one  
according to whatever scheme you like.  You could do this using a for  
loop, and the "degree" function in sna could provide the relevant node  
degrees at each iteration.

Dave

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Possible bug w/centralization function?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Statnet Help,

I'm trying to get the betweenness centralization scores for some 
undirected networks, and have run into a problem.  The result of the 
command (centralization(NetworkObj, betweenness, mode="graph", 
normalize=TRUE)) on my data is incorrect.  It is exactly half of what it 
should be when I calculate betweenness centralization by hand.

I have discovered that if I instead use the command for a directed 
network (centralization(NetworkObj, betweenness, mode="digraph", 
normalize=TRUE)) it does give the right number.  But, that shouldn't be, 
since I do not have a directed network.

By contrast, when I run the two commands on an older version of R (with 
older versions of SNA and Network), the results are correct.  Is this a 
bug in the new version?

Output txt files attached -- one file showing output under current 
version of statnet, and another file showing output under previous 
package versions.

thanks!
Natalie Cotton

PhD Student, Univ. of Michigan


--

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Possible bug w/centralization function?
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Natalie -

Natalie C. Cotton wrote:
> Hi Statnet Help,
> 
> I'm trying to get the betweenness centralization scores for some 
> undirected networks, and have run into a problem.  The result of the 
> command (centralization(NetworkObj, betweenness, mode="graph", 
> normalize=TRUE)) on my data is incorrect.  It is exactly half of what it 
> should be when I calculate betweenness centralization by hand.
> 
> I have discovered that if I instead use the command for a directed 
> network (centralization(NetworkObj, betweenness, mode="digraph", 
> normalize=TRUE)) it does give the right number.  But, that shouldn't be, 
> since I do not have a directed network.
> 
> By contrast, when I run the two commands on an older version of R (with 
> older versions of SNA and Network), the results are correct.  Is this a 
> bug in the new version?

Looks like the new version introduced an inconsistency in how 
directedness is handled in the centralization normalization for 
betweenness when cmode is left at its default value ("directed").  You 
can force the expected behavior with

centralization(NetworkObj, betweenness, mode="graph",
cmode="undirected")

(However, you can get the same answer by treating the network as 
directed, since this multiplies the numerator and the denominator by the 
same amount.  So centralization(NetworkObj,betweenness) will also work 
for undirected data.)

Thanks for the bug report.  A fix will go out in the next revision,

-Carter
